extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: The first environment for training software engineering (SWE) agents. SWE-Gym contains 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.citeAs: Pan, J., Wang, X., Neubig, G., Jaitly, N., Ji, H., Suhr, A., & Zhang, Y. (2025). Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym. Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We first use SEART GitHub search to filter a list of initial repositories. We select Python repositories that were created before July 1, 2022 and have more than 500 stars, with at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests and 100 contributors. We use SWE-Bench’s instance extraction script to convert these repositories into task instances. We manually configure dependencies for each task instance using relevant configuration files. We then use SWE-Bench’s execution-based validation script to ensure that the gold patch passes more unit tests than the original code.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: After validation and filtering out failed instances, we obtained 2,438 unit-test-validated instances from 11 repositories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: SWE-Gym Raw, a large set of Python GitHub issues without executable environments (64,689 instances spanning 358 Python repositories).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We generalize SWE-Bench’s versioning script to support versioning via script execution, and semi-automatically collect versions for each instance based on information available in the repository. We manually configure dependencies for each task instance using relevant configuration files.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We use SWE-Bench’s instance extraction script to convert these repositories into task instances. We use SWE-Bench’s execution-based validation script to ensure that the gold patch passes more unit tests than the original code, filtering out failed instances. SWE-Gym Lite excludes tasks that require editing more than one file, tasks with poorly described problem statements, those with excessively complex ground-truth code diffs, and tests focused on error message validation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: This process required approximately 200 human annotation hours and 10,000 CPU core hours. Annotations are done by a subset of the authors. The annotation involved manually configuring dependencies and semi-automatically collecting versions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: After validation and filtering out failed instances, we obtained 2,438 unit-test-validated instances from 11 repositories.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SWE-Bench’s instance extraction script, SWE-Bench’s versioning script, SWE-Bench’s execution-based validation script
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer’s productivity and accessibility across industries. As these agents become more capable, they may impact software engineering jobs and require careful consideration around code ownership, licensing, and attribution. Additionally, similar techniques could potentially be misused to automate the creation of malicious code.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Data Bias Impacts Performance. Repeated sampling shows that task success probability follows a long-tail distribution, where more samples increase solved instances. While broader task coverage benefits training, it introduces a bias toward easier tasks. Ignoring executable environments could introduce distribution bias. The task distribution across repositories exhibits a long-tail pattern; tasks associated with pandas comprise nearly one-third of the total, whereas tasks related to bokeh represent a mere one percent.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: SWE-Gym is limited by its environment diversity, including the number of repositories, types of tasks, and programming languages. SWE-Gym Raw instances do not contain executable environments or a guarantee that its unit tests are effective in evaluating the correctness of a solution. Self-improvement results are modest.
